claims.text: Low hardness and strength in equimolar or near-equimolar CoCrFeNiTi are governed by the absence of significant precipitation or ordering.
The relevant starting state is a single-phase FCC or BCC solid solution.
The single-phase state has minimal lattice distortion and weak solid-solution strengthening.
Structural simplicity permits easy dislocation motion.
Easy dislocation motion produces favorable plasticity and machinability while limiting hardness and strength.
As-cast or homogenized equimolar or near-equimolar CoCrFeNiTi can provide a single-phase state without significant precipitates or ordering.
Aging or annealing can induce secondary-phase precipitation or ordered-phase formation in the same alloy.
Precipitates or ordered phases increase obstacles to dislocation motion.
Increasing obstacles to dislocation motion by precipitation or ordering raises hardness and strength.
Single-phase CoCrFeNiTi will have lower hardness and yield strength than composition-matched precipitated or ordered CoCrFeNiTi.
The single-phase state is predicted to have Vickers hardness below 250 HV.
The single-phase state is predicted to have yield strength below 500 MPa.
The proposed hardness and strength values are typical of ductile FCC high-entropy alloys.
The hypothesis applies to equimolar or near-equimolar CoCrFeNiTi with grain size greater than 10 micrometers under room-temperature, quasi-static loading.
The hypothesis does not apply to heavily deformed, nanocrystalline, multiphase, or ordered starting states.
Minor compositional deviations or processing history may change the strengthening effect size.
